holidays.name: National Almond Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the humble almond by snacking on them roasted, salted, chocolate-covered, or blitzed into milk and butter. Almond lovers everywhere crunch in unison.
holidays.origin: Part of the many unofficial American food days popularized by food industry groups and snack enthusiasts. The exact founder is unclear, but the almond has been cultivated for thousands of years and California now grows most of the world's supply.
holidays.funFact: Almonds aren't true nuts. They're the seeds of a fruit related to peaches, plums, and cherries. California's almond orchards supply roughly 80 percent of the world's almonds.

holidays.name: Do a Grouch a Favor Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to being kind to the cranky, crotchety, and curmudgeonly people in your life. The idea is that a small good deed might crack a grumpy facade, or at least confuse the grouch in a delightful way.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that sits right after Valentine's Day, the idea being that those who felt left out of the love fest could use a little kindness. It has been listed in quirky holiday calendars for years.
holidays.funFact: Studies on kindness suggest that doing nice things for others boosts your own mood too, so the grouch might not be the only one who benefits.

holidays.name: Innocence Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek celebration of the innocent side of life. People are encouraged to embrace childlike wonder, play, and wide-eyed curiosity, or at least to plead innocent about something.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance from the world of quirky calendars, often paired with the reflective mood that follows Valentine's Day. Its creator is not clearly documented.
holidays.funFact: The word innocent comes from the Latin innocens, meaning harmless or not hurting. Not guilty is a very different legal idea from innocent, which explains why courts say not guilty.

holidays.name: Tim Tam Day
holidays.description: A day for Australia's famous chocolate biscuit fans to indulge in the beloved treat, including the legendary Tim Tam Slam, where you bite off opposite corners and use the biscuit as a straw for hot chocolate or coffee.
holidays.origin: Tim Tams were created by Arnott's in Australia in 1964 after Ian Norris, a company executive, tried a British biscuit called the Penguin and vowed to make a better one. Fans have since turned it into an informal celebration.
holidays.funFact: The biscuit was named after the winning horse of the 1958 Kentucky Derby, Tim Tam. Arnott's sells millions of packs a year in Australia.

holidays.name: Public Sleeping Day (Unofficial)
holidays.description: A cozy day for catching a nap wherever you happen to be, from park benches to office chairs, for those who believe a nap is a human right.
holidays.origin: Quirky holiday lists often feature nap-related observances in the winter, when daylight is short and energy is low. This one is informal and has no official founder.
holidays.funFact: Many cultures have a tradition of midday napping, such as the Spanish siesta, and research suggests short naps of 10 to 20 minutes can boost alertness and performance.
